bc_pulpit_rock.blurb: Pulpit Rock is the cliff above Nelson in the West Kootenay that most people know as a hiking destination, and it also holds a dozen bolted and traditional lines. Ten of the twelve are sport and two are trad, with the grade spread centred on 5.10, a couple of 5.9s, and single climbs in the 5.11 and 5.12 range. The best-known lines are multi-pitch, running three to six pitches, so it suits parties wanting a longer day rather than a quick lap. Expect a steep talus approach below the face, and carry a pad or sling for the awkward belay ledge at the foot.

bc_the_back_side.blurb: The Back Side is a small boulder cluster tucked behind the main forest zone of The Grid, in the Hunter Creek valley near Hope in the Fraser Valley. It holds twelve problems and nothing else, with a spread from easy V0 through the mid grades to a couple of V6s. Most problems fall between V2 and V5, so it works for a mixed group more than for a pure beginner or a pure project session. The forest setting around The Grid means sandy-floored landings are typical of the neighbourhood, and it makes a natural add-on to a day on the larger sectors nearby.

bc_green_eggs_and_sam.blurb: Green Eggs and Sam is the main cluster of the East Side Boulders at Cypress Falls Park in West Vancouver, a creek-canyon trail system close to the city. Twelve problems sit here, all on the easy end: five at V0 or below, four at V1, a single V2 and two V3s. That makes it a good first outing for newer boulderers and a quick session for anyone after warm-ups. Reaching it means following the trail beyond the Simian area to an obvious group of blocks on the slope above, with a lone boulder first and the rest a short way further up. The canyon stays cool in summer.

bc_klondike_boulders.blurb: Klondike Boulders is a forested bouldering zone in the Fraser Canyon, part of the Gold Rush area between Yale and Spuzzum. The ground is a mix of shaded woods and talus, and the blocks are reported to dry quickly and to stay climbable through light precipitation. Twelve problems are recorded, running from V0 up to V5 or V6, with the bulk in the middle: roughly V2 to V5, and V3 being the most common grade. The first problems lie a short walk uphill from the roadside lot, so it suits a quick stop on a longer Fraser Canyon day.

bc_burning_man_corner_north.blurb: Burning Man Corner (North) is a short wall of pale, clean rock just left of The Zip in the Smoke Bluffs, on the edge of Squamish. About twenty-three metres tall, it carries twelve routes, eight trad and four sport, mostly between 5.7 and 5.10, with five at 5.10 and one 5.11. That spread makes it friendly for climbers moving up from 5.8 and 5.9 onto the harder grades, with gear placements to build skills and a few bolted lines for variety. The crag shares its approach with The Zip nearby, so the two are easy to combine.

bc_quercus_cliff.blurb: Quercus Cliff is a single wall in Murrin Park, just off the Loop Trail south of Squamish, sitting in a cleared nook above Lakeside in the Woods. It carries twelve lines, split evenly between sport and trad, and it is a crag for strong climbers: a few 5.10s and 5.11s open the range, but most routes sit at 5.12 and above, topping out in the 5.13s and a single 5.14. Several lines blend bolts with gear, and some are extensions of others. Plan on stiff, technical climbing rather than an easy mileage day.
